title: What is six Hundredths shared into five equal parts?
description: Zero point zero six is divided by five place by place. The Ones and Tenths give zero each, and the six Hundredths are shared and regrouped into Thousandths. Keeko's doubt is that the digits one and two can be read as Tenths and Hundredths.
teaching_notes: One idea: each digit of the answer is written in the place it was shared in, so a share of Thousandths belongs three places after the point. Watch for students who write the answer digits too far left.

video_script.why: The child shares whole numbers well but writes the answer digits in the wrong places when the number is a small decimal.
video_script.substitution: Each digit of the answer is written in the place that was shared: Ones, Tenths, Hundredths, Thousandths.
video_script.anchor: Zero point zero six, divided into five equal parts
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko finds the digits one and two but writes them as one Tenth and two Hundredths, so the answer is ten times too big.
video_script.payoff_line: Zero point zero six divided by five is zero point zero one two.
video_script.design: The place columns stay on the board; each digit of the answer lands in the column of the place that was shared.

beats.on_screen: title card From your book; place columns Ones, Tenths, Hundredths, Thousandths with 0.06 written and 5 equal parts drawn

marks.num: zero point zero six appears in the columns with five equal parts beside it

narration: <bookmark mark='scene'/>This is an example from your book about dividing a small decimal.
<bookmark mark='num'/>The number is zero point zero six, and it is divided into five equal parts.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>What is zero point zero six divided by five?

beats.on_screen: the place columns and the five parts stay on the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: Columns Ones, Tenths, Hundredths, Thousandths; each share is written in the column of the place it came from

marks.cols: the four columns are lined up after the decimal point
marks.rule: an arrow shows each share going to the same column as the place it came from

narration: <bookmark mark='cols'/>After the decimal point come the Tenths, the Hundredths and then the Thousandths.
<bookmark mark='rule'/>Each share is written in the column of the place that was shared.

beats.on_screen: Given: 0 Ones + 0 Tenths + 6 Hundredths, divided into 5 equal parts
narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, no Ones, no Tenths and six Hundredths, to be divided into five equal parts.

beats.on_screen: To find: what one of the 5 equal parts is

marks.find: the share of one part is outlined

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find how much one of the five equal parts gets.

beats.on_screen: 0 Ones ÷ 5 = 0 Ones; point placed; 0 Tenths ÷ 5 = 0 Tenths

marks.s1a: zero Ones are shared and a zero is written
marks.s1b: the decimal point is placed and zero Tenths give a zero

narration: <bookmark mark='s1a'/>Step one, share the big places. Zero Ones divided by five gives zero Ones.
<bookmark mark='s1b'/>Place the decimal point. Zero Tenths divided by five gives zero Tenths.

marks.s2b: one Hundredth goes to each part and one Hundredth remains

narration: <bookmark mark='s2a'/>Step two, share the Hundredths. We have six Hundredths.
<bookmark mark='s2b'/>Six Hundredths divided by five gives one Hundredth for each part, and one Hundredth remains.

marks.s3a: the Hundredth that remains breaks into ten Thousandths
marks.s3b: two Thousandths go to each part

narration: <bookmark mark='s3a'/>Step three, regroup the leftover Hundredth into ten Thousandths.
<bookmark mark='s3b'/>Ten Thousandths divided by five gives two Thousandths for each part.

beats.on_screen: Each part: 0 Ones, 0 Tenths, 1 Hundredth, 2 Thousandths = ?

marks.s4a: the shares of one part are lined up in their columns
marks.s4b: the number they make is left blank

narration: <bookmark mark='s4a'/>Step four, put each share in its own column.
<bookmark mark='s4b'/>Each part has no Ones, no Tenths, one Hundredth and two Thousandths.
<bookmark mark='ans'/>Zero point zero six divided by five is zero point zero one two.

beats.on_screen: Keeko with a raised hand beside the place columns
narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: Keeko's bubble shows 0.12; a check 0.12 × 5 = 0.6 is written and the 0.6 is much bigger than 0.06; the bubble is crossed out and the 1 and 2 slide one column to the right

marks.fix: five times the bubble number is worked out and is ten times too big
marks.right: the one and the two slide to the Hundredths and Thousandths columns

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks the answer is zero point one two. The one and the two sit next to the point.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>But five times zero point one two is zero point six. That is ten times the number we began with.
<bookmark mark='right'/>Write each share in the column of the place it came from. The one belongs in the Hundredths, and the two belongs in the Thousandths.
